meta.title: Different Prizes
meta.textType: story: what two children like, from pictures

paragraphs: On Friday, Teacher Kim's class has a quiz. The quiz has twenty questions about animals, space, and food. Mia and Leo get every answer right. The class claps for them. Teacher Kim says, "Come to the table, and choose a prize." There are six prizes on the table. There is a lovely book about animals, a funny hat, and a puzzle. There is also a chess set, a magazine, and a cartoon book. "You can look at each prize, if you want," says Teacher Kim.

Mia stops at the book about animals. It has a pretty cat on the cover. She looks at it for a long time. Leo laughs and puts on the funny hat. Lily watches them from her desk. She smiles at her friends. "Mia might choose the book, and Leo might choose the hat," says Lily. Mia smiles and holds the book close.

Teacher Kim asks, "What do you prefer, Mia?" Mia answers first. "I like cartoons, but I prefer books about animals," says Mia. "Animals are interesting, and I hate chess." Teacher Kim turns to Leo, and Leo stands up. "I want to be an actor," he says. "I prefer the funny hat, and I hate puzzles." Everyone laughs.

So each child has a different prize. Mia takes the book, and Leo takes the hat. They hold up the prizes and smile, and Teacher Kim claps. "Which prize do you prefer, Teacher Kim?" asks Lily. "I prefer the puzzle," says Teacher Kim, "but I might read the magazine, too." Leo says, "I might wear my hat in a school play." Each child is happy with the prize. It is a good day.
text.summary: Teacher Kim's class has a quiz. Mia and Leo choose different prizes from a table, and Lily guesses what each child likes.
